reason: Awn-tipped means the apex ends in an awn. That is the same reading as the earlier aristate rule C207 (awn present), with the apex as the part of the bearer.
A thin blade or petal is thin in substance. No texture class is named, so the safe reading is thickness.
Pinninerved means veined in a pinnate pattern, the existing FLOPO class.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum of two values: cylindrical PATO_0001873 – campanulate PATO_0104350)
reason: A compound of two shape values that both exist, like oblong-ovate. It needs the continuum pattern, not a new term.
Margins rolled under, towards the lower side, are revolute.
Leathery but thinner than fully coriaceous. This matches the definition of subcoriaceous ('somewhat leathery but less thick or rigid').
Glossaries give pilulose as minutely pilose, with very small fine hairs. That falls under puberulous; it should not be confused with pilular (ball-shaped).
French 'fauve' is fawn or tawny. config/botanical_colour_synonyms.tsv already maps fawn to the backbone class brown as a NARROW synonym.
Native says where a taxon comes from (its distribution status). It is not a phenotype of the plant.

label: prorulose
definition: A texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's cells having their ends projecting as low, papilla-like protrusions (prorulae) above the surface.
reason: A standard term in moss descriptions. Moss floras keep prorulae (projecting cell ends) apart from papillae (outgrowths over the cell lumen), so it is a sibling of FLOPO:0991059 papillose, not a synonym.
A stegocarpic moss capsule has a separate lid (operculum) that comes off to open it. That is the presence of the PO spore capsule operculum.

label: septifragal
definition: A dehiscent quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's opening at maturity by valves that break away from the septa, the septa remaining attached to the central axis.
reason: A standard type of capsule opening, a sibling of FLOPO:0991151 septicidal and FLOPO:0991152 loculicidal. The 'septicides' examples belong to the existing septicidal rule.

label: monoicous
definition: A phenotypic sex quality inhering in a bryophyte gametophyte by virtue of its bearing both antheridia and archegonia on the same individual.
reason: The moss and liverwort term covering autoicous, paroicous and synoicous. FLOPO:0991071 monoecious is defined for seed plants, and FLOPO:0991093 autoicous is narrower; autoicous should become a child of monoicous.
Flexuous maps to sinuous (rule C190), so this is its negation.
Glumes and lemmas without keels are not carinate (carinate maps to keel-shaped, rule C221). The PO class keel PO_0025327 is the Fabaceae petal keel, so it cannot be used here.
Lanuginous means woolly; PATO lanate has woolly as a synonym.
A bunchgrass grows in a dense tuft from the base, which is the caespitose (tufted, clump-forming) habit.
Lophate spores and pollen carry raised ridges (lophae) on the wall. Ridged is the existing quality; the finer palynological sense of ridges around hollows is not needed for these statements.
A count of ovules (plant ovule PO_0020003), like 'few-flowered': the counted part is in the word.
Inermous (unarmed) means without spines, prickles or thorns. One negation of spiny covers all three better than three absence rules.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum of two values: bristly PATO_0104117 – strigose FLOPO:0991086)
reason: A compound of two hair-cover values that both have terms. It needs the continuum pattern, not a new class.
Same reading as 'without keels': not carinate.
A spelling variant of the existing class.
A spelling variant of the existing class.
Exalbuminous seeds lack endosperm; PO lists albumen as a synonym of endosperm.

label: doubly serrate
definition: A serrated quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's margin bearing large forward-pointing teeth that are themselves serrate.
reason: A standard margin type that serrated alone does not express, and that neither FLOPO:0991081 serrulate nor a count captures.

label: rhizautoicous
definition: An autoicous quality inhering in a bryophyte gametophyte by virtue of its male branches or dwarf male shoots being connected to the female stem only by rhizoids.
reason: A recognised kind of autoicy in moss floras, 46 statements in 3 floras. It sits below the existing autoicous class.

label: medial (sensu botany)
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being located about midway between the midrib and the margin of the structure that bears it.
reason: Position of fern sori between costa and margin, a sibling of FLOPO:0991208 marginal. PATO_0001191 'medial to' is relational and anatomical; supramedial and inframedial would be its neighbours.

label: systylious
definition: A structural quality inhering in a moss spore capsule by virtue of its operculum remaining attached to the top of the columella after dehiscence and being raised with it.
reason: A standard moss capsule character with no PATO or FLOPO term. As a relation it would need an attachment after dehiscence that the relation pattern does not cover.

Moss cell walls, trigones and exothecial cells that are 'not bulging' are not convex, which negates the shape the floras contrast it with. The bearer is often an unground cell part, so many rows will stay unresolved.
